optionReasons.saa-ini-140:option:0: Elastic IP by instance EXPOSES the instances and does not change the route of traffic to S3.
optionReasons.saa-ini-140:option:1: NAT the larger the bandwidth, but the cost per GB processed and the route via the internet CONTINUAM.
optionReasons.saa-ini-140:option:2: The S3 does not live 'in another VPC' — peering is not the way to regional services of AWS.

finalJustifications: Because the Gateway Endpoint to S3 in the route table keeps traffic within the network of AWS — no NAT, no internet, no cost per hour or per GB.
Because Gateway Endpoint compresses data before sending it to S3, cutting the volume processed and the cost per GB.
Because the Gateway Endpoint creates a replica of the bucket inside the VPC, Serving readings without leaving the private network.
Because the Gateway Endpoint collects 50% less than or NAT Gateway by GB, and the economy pays for the change of architecture.

optionReasons.saa-ini-161:option:0: The CloudTrail REGISTRA calls from API — does not analyze or detect threats alone.
optionReasons.saa-ini-161:option:1: The Config evaluates CONFORMIDADE configuration — does not detect malicious behavior.
optionReasons.saa-ini-161:option:3: The Inspector evaluation VULNERABILIDADES Software (CVEs) — does not monitor malicious activity in logs.

finalJustifications: Because GuardDuty is the detection of managed threats: analysis CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs with ML and thread intel — crypt mining, malicious IPs, anonymous APIs — no agents.
Because GuardDuty automatically closes the instances committed to mining, containing the incident before the security team response.
Because GuardDuty requires the agent of the SSM in all monitored instances — it is he who collects the signs of commitment analyzed by the service.
Because GuardDuty analyzes only the management account of the organization, consolidating the threats of all member accounts via delegation.

optionReasons.saa-ini-165:option:0: The CloudWatch Logs is the DESTINO where logs are stored — does not capture network traffic alone.
optionReasons.saa-ini-165:option:1: X-Ray tracks REQUIREMENTS between microservices — non-IP traffic of network interfaces.
optionReasons.saa-ini-165:option:2: The CloudTrail records calls from API — no network connections with IPs, ports and accept/reject.

finalJustifications: Because the VPC Flow Logs capture interface IP traffic metadata (origin, destination, ports, protocol), ACCEPT/REJECT) — without the payload of the packages.
Because the VPC Flow Logs record the full contents of packages for forensic analysis, including suspicious payload.
Because the VPC Flow Logs automatically lock detected suspicious IPs, cutting communication in the interface.
Because the VPC Flow Logs only monitor traffic that crosses the Internet Gateway, where the external IP would be seen.

optionReasons.saa-ini-170:option:0: Security Groups filter by port/protocol/origin POR INSTANCE — without filtering by domain or IDS/IPS.
optionReasons.saa-ini-170:option:2: NACLs are statesss and limited to simple IP/port rules by sub-network — no intrusion signatures.
optionReasons.saa-ini-170:option:3: The WAF ProtectS APPLICATIONS WEB (HTTP in ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway) — does not associate with sub-networks or inspects general network traffic.

finalJustifications: Because Network Firewall is stateful managed network firewall: domain filtering, rules IDS/IPS and own rules, applied centrally to the traffic of VPCs.
Because Network Firewall runs like an agent within each instance EC2, inspecting traffic before leaving the machine.
Because Network Firewall is the paid version of NACLs, with more rules per sub-network and status evaluation of active connections.
Because Network Firewall only filters traffic HTTPS of the VPCs, delegating the other protocols to the NACLs and Security Groups.

optionReasons.saa-ini-173:option:0: Internet Gateway exposes the VPC on the Internet — exactly what you don't want.
optionReasons.saa-ini-173:option:2: The NAT Gateway would solve, but routing the traffic to the INTERNET and at cost — the team discarded this option.
optionReasons.saa-ini-173:option:3: There's no such thing as 'VPC Peering with the account of AWS' — the services do not live in VPC Payable.

finalJustifications: Because Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) create private ENIs at VPC to call the APIs SSM and KMS directly — traffic never leaves the network of AWS.
Because Interface Endpoints copy the APIs of SSM and KMS within the VPC, responding locally to calls.
Because Interface Endpoints establish a VPN managed up to each service, with dedicated encrypted tunnels.
Because Interface Endpoints are free like Gateway Endpoints, and the economy is the reason to use them instead of the NAT.

optionReasons.saa-ini-174:option:0: The EC2 Connect Forum requires door 22 ABERTA — violates the policy.
optionReasons.saa-ini-174:option:1: Direct Connect is corporate physical connectivity — does not eliminate the need for open door to SSH.
optionReasons.saa-ini-174:option:3: Bastion host is PROIBIDO by policy — even restricted to corporate IPs, still being door 22 exposed.

finalJustifications: Because Session Manager gives interactive shell via agent SSM SEM open entry doors with recorded audit sessions — meets the entire policy.
Because Session Manager opens the door 22 only during the active session and the close automatically when closing the access.
Because Session Manager uses an instance output connection directly to the authorized operator station.
Because Session Manager works only in instances with public IP, where session log can be routed.

optionReasons.saa-ini-188:option:0: Making the sub-network public EXPOSUREs instances — exchange of costs for unacceptable risk.
optionReasons.saa-ini-188:option:1: NAT the biggest can handle more band, but the TAXA POR Continued processing GB — cost remains.
optionReasons.saa-ini-188:option:2: Compression reduces volume, but traffic continues to cross (and pay) the NAT.

finalJustifications: Because the Gateway Endpoint to S3 runs direct traffic through the network of the AWS, outside NAT — the data processing rate of the NAT for this traffic simply disappears.
Because Gateway Endpoint transfers the processing cost of NAT for the bucket itself S3, diluted in storage rate.
Because the Gateway Endpoint hides the most read objects in the private subnet, and the hits stop generating traffic charged on NAT.
Because the Gateway Endpoint gives 50% discount rate on the NAT Gateway for traffic intended for internal services of its own AWS.

optionReasons.saa-ini-206:option:1: The Security Group new now PERMITE all output by default — not typical lock.
optionReasons.saa-ini-206:option:2: There is no restriction of AZ in DynamoDB — the service is REGIONAL.
optionReasons.saa-ini-206:option:3: Lack of permission IAM generates AUTHORIZATION error (AccessDenied) — the symptom described is a failure of CONECTIVIDADE (timeout).

finalJustifications: Because DynamoDB is accessed by public endpoint: private sub-network without NAT or VPC Endpoint has no route to it — the calls give timeout; the solution is the Gateway Endpoint (free of charge).).
Because DynamoDB needs to be installed inside the VPC application, as a cluster managed with local endpoints by private sub-network.
Because DynamoDB rejects connections from private IPs for security — only public addresses go through service validation.
Because DynamoDB requires HTTPS in calls and private sub-networks only speak HTTP — o TLS requires a public certificate issued on the edge.
